games.title: Spacewar!
games.note: Written for the PDP-1 at MIT; two ships duel around a star whose gravity pulls them in.

games.title: Star Control
games.dev: Toys for Bob (Paul Reiche III, Fred Ford)
games.note: Fred Ford said 'StarCon is really just Archon with an S-T in front of it'.

games.title: Star Control II
games.note: An open galaxy of alien races to meet; its code was later released as the free Ur-Quan Masters.

games.title: Archon
games.note: A chess-like board where every capture is fought out as a real-time arcade duel; Paul Reiche III co-designed it.

games.title: Traveller
games.note: A science-fiction pen-and-paper RPG of traders, mercenaries and starship crews.

games.title: Wing Commander
games.note: Chris Roberts's space dogfighter with a branching campaign; its cat-like Kilrathi were inspired by Larry Niven's Kzinti.

games.title: Wing Commander III: Heart of the Tiger
games.note: Told its story through full-motion video starring Mark Hamill, Malcolm McDowell and John Rhys-Davies.

games.title: Wing Commander: Privateer
games.note: An open-ended spin-off where you trade, hunt bounties or turn pirate in the Gemini Sector.

games.title: Starlancer
games.note: A mission-based space combat game set in a 22nd-century war between rival alliances.

games.title: Freelancer
games.note: Chris Roberts began it as a galaxy that keeps running whether or not you are there; Microsoft finished it.

games.title: Star Citizen
games.note: Crowdfunded since 2012 and playable as an unfinished alpha since its 2013 hangar module.

games.title: Elite Dangerous
games.note: Kickstarted in 2012 by David Braben; it recreates the Milky Way at full scale.

games.title: X: Beyond the Frontier
games.note: The first game in Egosoft's X series of space trading and building sims.

games.title: Space Rangers
games.note: A Russian mix of turn-based space trading, combat and text adventure quests.

games.title: Battlecruiser 3000AD
games.note: Derek Smart's ambitious capital-ship sim, released in 1996 after years of delays.

games.title: Battlehawks 1942
games.note: Lawrence Holland's first WWII air-combat sim, set over the Pacific in 1942.

games.title: Secret Weapons of the Luftwaffe
games.note: The last of Holland's WWII flight sims, with late-war German jets, before he moved on to X-Wing.

games.title: Star Wars (1983 arcade)
games.note: A color vector-graphics cockpit game ending in the Death Star trench run, with digitized voices from the film.

games.title: Starglider
games.note: Jez San's fast 3D wireframe shooter for 16-bit home computers.

games.title: Star Wars: Squadrons
games.note: A cockpit-only space combat game, playable in VR, whose campaign alternates New Republic and Imperial pilots.

games.title: Everspace
games.note: A roguelike space shooter from Rockfish, founded by Fishlabs founders Michael Schade and Christian Lohr.

games.title: FTL: Faster Than Light
games.note: Two developers' roguelike about managing a starship's crew and systems, funded on Kickstarter.

games.title: Outer Wilds
games.note: Began as Alex Beachum's student thesis project at USC.

games.title: Starfield
games.note: Bethesda's first new universe in 25 years; a PlayStation 5 version followed in April 2026.

games.title: Kerbal Space Program
games.note: Build rockets for little green Kerbals; named after tin figures its creator put inside fireworks as a teenager.

games.title: Kerbal Space Program 2
games.note: Launched in early access in 2023; its studio was shut down the following year.

games.title: Flight Simulator
games.note: Bruce Artwick's early home-computer flight simulator, the basis for Microsoft Flight Simulator.

games.title: Microsoft Flight Simulator (1982)
games.note: Released for the IBM PC in November 1982; PC makers used it to test IBM compatibility.

games.title: Microsoft Flight Simulator (2020)
games.note: Streams the whole Earth from Bing Maps data, with buildings generated by machine learning from satellite images.

games.title: Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024
games.note: Added career jobs such as firefighting, crop dusting and search and rescue.

games.title: Air Combat
games.note: Known as Ace Combat in Japan; the first home game in the series.

games.title: Ace Combat 04: Shattered Skies
games.note: Told its war story through illustrated cutscenes about a boy in an occupied town.

games.title: Ace Combat 7: Skies Unknown
games.note: Added clouds that hide enemies and ice up your jet, plus PlayStation VR missions.

games.title: Project Wingman
games.note: A Kickstarter-funded arcade flight game made by a tiny independent team.

games.title: Journey
games.note: Strangers can meet online in its desert but can talk only through musical chimes.

games.title: No Man's Sky
games.note: Its universe of about 18 quintillion planets disappointed many at launch; years of free updates won players back.

links.took: Two-ship duels with inertia around a planet's gravity well.
links.added: Many alien ship designs with special weapons, set inside a strategy campaign.

links.extra: Created by Paul Reiche III and Fred Ford.

links.added: Starships and alien species in place of chess-like fantasy pieces.

links.took: The ship-versus-ship melee combat and alien races.

links.took: The default commander name, Jameson, from the RPG Ian Bell played.

links.took: The Flight Simulator name and its aim of realistic civil flying.
links.added: The entire planet streamed from map data, with live weather and air traffic.

links.took: The streamed whole-Earth world and Asobo's engine.
links.added: Career missions such as firefighting, aerial tours and search and rescue.

links.took: Mining, trading, missions and pirate fights; CCP's developers said EVE evolved from Elite.
links.added: One shared online universe where players run corporations, wars and the economy.

src.t: Wikipedia: Eve Online (CCP developers)
Wikipedia: Elite (CCP's senior producers cited Elite)

links.extra: David Braben has called EVE a reimplementation of Elite rather than its true successor.

links.took: Multiplayer chat and open player-versus-player conflict.

src.t: Wikipedia: Eve Online (CCP developers)

links.extra: CCP described EVE as Elite's concepts combined with Ultima Online's multiplayer chat and player-versus-player play.

links.took: A procedurally generated galaxy to explore freely; Elite was a big part of Murray's childhood.
links.added: Seamless landings on planets with their own generated plants and animals.

src.t: Wikipedia: Development of No Man's Sky
Sean Murray, interview, Vice Motherboard

links.extra: Murray: 'Elite was procedurally generated, and so were lots of games at the time, like Star Control and Freelancer.'

links.took: The feeling of exploring a vast galaxy of strange worlds and aliens.
links.added: Quintillions of planets you can fly down to and walk on.

src.t: Wikipedia: Development of No Man's Sky

links.took: Freely flying between star systems to trade and fight.
links.added: Survival crafting on foot and endless procedurally made worlds.

src.t: Wikipedia: Development of No Man's Sky

links.took: Simple, elegant design built around wonder rather than instructions.
links.added: A whole universe of planets, with survival, crafting and trading.

src.t: Wikipedia: Development of No Man's Sky

links.took: Cockpit space-combat conventions that historians say Star Raiders established.
links.added: Cinematic missions with wingmen and a branching war story.

src.t: Wikipedia: Star Raiders (cites Barton and Loguidice)

links.took: Cinematic cockpit space combat with a mission-based story campaign.
links.added: Star Wars ships and a flight model shaped by Holland's WWII sims.

Wikipedia: Wing Commander (led to rivals such as X-Wing)

links.extra: A 1992 preview said the developers were 'taking aim at Chris Roberts and his megahit Wing Commander series'.

links.took: First-person space combat against enemy fighters.
links.added: Star Wars missions, power management and a full story campaign.

src.t: Wikipedia: Star Wars: X-Wing (drew some influence from Star Raiders)

links.took: Lawrence Holland's WWII air-combat simulation and mission design.
links.added: The European air war, including experimental German jets.

src.t: Wikipedia: Secret Weapons of the Luftwaffe (Lawrence Holland)

links.took: Holland's experience building WWII air-combat simulators.
links.added: Space combat in the Star Wars universe, with shields and laser power management.

src.t: Wikipedia: Star Wars: X-Wing (Holland's earlier WWII air-combat sims)

links.took: The war with the cat-like Kilrathi and cinematic space combat.
links.added: Full-motion video scenes with Mark Hamill and fully 3D ships.

links.took: Wing Commander's flight engine and universe.
links.added: Open-ended trading, bounty hunting and piracy instead of a military campaign.

links.took: Open-ended space trading, piracy and ship upgrades.
links.added: Wing Commander's graphics and a story campaign you can follow or ignore.

src.t: Wikipedia: Elite (a model for Privateer, Freelancer and EVE Online)

links.took: Trading, bounty hunting and freely roaming between star systems.
links.added: Mouse-driven flight, a cinematic story and a galaxy that runs without you.

src.t: Wikipedia: Elite (a model for Privateer, Freelancer and EVE Online)

links.took: Chris Roberts's space-combat experience; the idea dated back to Wing Commander.
links.added: A living galaxy whose factions and traffic carry on whether you are there or not.

src.t: Wikipedia: Freelancer

links.took: Digital Anvil's setting; Freelancer is a chronological sequel to Starlancer.
links.added: Open-ended trading and exploration instead of linear combat missions.

src.t: Wikipedia: Freelancer

links.took: Cinematic space combat; Roberts calls Star Citizen a spiritual successor to Wing Commander.
links.added: Seamless walking, flying and landing in one crowdfunded online universe.

src.t: Wikipedia: Star Citizen (Chris Roberts)

links.took: Roberts's unrealized plans for a living galaxy, retried at a larger scale.
links.added: First-person movement inside ships and across planets.

src.t: Wikipedia: Star Citizen (Chris Roberts)

links.extra: Wikipedia describes the game as an extended retry of unrealized plans for Freelancer.

links.took: Trading and freelancing careers, promised in the Kickstarter pitch.
links.added: Persistent online trade routes, cargo ships and multi-crew vessels.

links.extra: The pitch promised 'everything that made Wing Commander and Privateer / Freelancer special'.

links.took: Realistic flight, real star maps and planet landings from Frontier.
links.added: Online play in a full-scale Milky Way.

links.took: Open-ended trading and fighting in space from a cockpit.
links.added: Buying factories to shape a living economy.

src.t: Wikipedia: Elite (a model for the X series)

links.took: Open-ended space trading, piracy and missions, which its developers credited to Elite.
links.added: Turn-based travel, text adventure quests and a galaxy that lives without you.

links.took: An open-ended space sim of trading and combat, credited by its developer to Elite.

links.took: Fast 3D vector graphics, from Jez San's love of the Star Wars coin-op.
links.added: A free-roaming battle over a planet on a home computer.

links.took: Argonaut's 3D know-how, which led to building the Super FX chip with Nintendo.
links.added: Filled polygons, animal pilots and Nintendo's on-rails level design.

src.t: Wikipedia: Starglider

links.took: Cockpit Star Wars dogfights with power management, popularized by Totally Games' series.
links.added: Online five-versus-five fleet battles and full VR support.

links.took: Run-based space adventures where death sends you back to the start, popularized by FTL.
links.added: Real-time 3D dogfights from the cockpit.

links.took: Arcade jet combat with big missile counts and many real aircraft.
links.added: A full story told through illustrated cutscenes, with a rival ace squadron.

links.took: The fictional Strangereal world and arcade dogfighting.
links.added: Weather and clouds that affect flying, plus VR missions.

links.took: Arcade jet combat and dramatic missions in the Ace Combat style.
links.added: Made by a tiny indie team, following a mercenary squadron, with VR support.

links.took: Bethesda Game Studios' team and engine; full development began after Fallout 4.

links.took: Characters who tell tales of distant places, enticing you to go and see them.
